newsitem.title: USA: Nationwide curbs insurance coverage in coastal areas.
newsitem.headline: Nationwide curbs insurance coverage in coastal areas.

text.p: Nationwide Insurance said Thursday that in the wake of Hurricane Fran it will further reduce sales of new property insurance policies in the coastal counties from Maine to Texas.
The decision will affect 17 states, which are susceptible to severe windstorms and hurricane losses, said Nationwide, the nation's fifth largest property-casualty insurance firm.

"This is an additional move by the company in its constant effort to manage growth in areas that are highly vulnerable to extraordinary property losses from severe windstorms and hurricanes," said Richard Crabtree, president and chief operating officer.
He said the property-casualty company has been limiting sales of new policies in coastal areas for some time.
"But losses we've sustained in Hurricane Fran reinforce the need for Nationwide to further limit growth of new property coverages in coastal areas," he said.
Crabtree said the changes won't affect existing customers, except possibly a small number with property on barrier islands or very close to coastlines.
Nationwide said the move will not halt sales in Florida but will mean no sales growth. It will replace business there as it expires on a one-for-one basis, the company said.
In other coastal regions, Nationwide said it will slow growth but not stop it.

The increased density and higher value of properties that lie in the path of destructive hurricanes and other violent storms is a major concern for Nationwide and the insurance industry, the company said.
Compounding the concern is the increasing frequency of storms along the Atlantic and Gulf seaboards, Nationwide said.
The company said that it will work with state insurance departments to obtain any needed statutory approvals.
Chief Financial Officer Robert Oakley said the company wanted to protect its "great financial strength" which includes a policyholder surplus of more than $5 billion.
Last month, Nationwide estimated its claims from Hurricane Fran could soar to $150 million.
Nationwide said the hardest-hit state was North Carolina, where it is the largest property-casualty insurer.
